name: Hook Leg and Take Back
summary: A back take after Buggy Choke needs a separate rear torso attachment; the original control alone does not establish hooks, a seatbelt or completed back control.
description: A back take after Buggy Choke needs a separate rear torso attachment; the original control alone does not establish hooks, a seatbelt or completed back control.
overview:
The initial Buggy Choke configuration must be identified before considering Back Control. The bottom player supplies the arm-and-leg loop around the opponent's head and one arm. It does not require a collar grip, a turtle ride, or trapping the opponent's arm alone across their own throat. The reviewed instruction does not establish a direct Buggy Choke-to-Back Control connection. Release the original lock safely and establish the destination's own prerequisites; do not treat these checkpoints as a demonstrated continuous entry.

The bottom player has turned partly toward the opponent and brought an arm past the head. Protect both the defender's neck and the attacker's knee. Do not pull the foot against a fixed knee, use a slam, or remain attached when lifted. Open the whole loop on any stop signal. Open the original connection before either partner turns, rises or changes the captured limb.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Kade and Tye Ruotolo — OG Buggy Choke](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zixbOyLpoOc); [Jay Rodriguez — three Buggy Choke mistakes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MjKERx4N4mY).

flashcards.question: Hook Leg and Take Back (Buggy holder): Where is the holder in the initial choke setup?
flashcards.answer: The bottom player has turned partly toward the opponent and brought an arm past the head.

plausible: Under side pin, turned from link
Beside them, both chests face mat
trap: Above their chest, arm toward knee

flashcards.answer: Protect both the defender's neck and the attacker's knee. Do not pull the foot against a fixed knee, use a slam, or remain attached when lifted. Open the whole loop on any stop signal.

plausible: Just hip frame, choke grip kept
Just hand clasp, elbow hooks leg
trap: Just leg pressure, hand link intact

flashcards.question: Hook Leg and Take Back (Buggy holder): What must open before a separate turn toward rear access?
flashcards.answer: Open the original connection before either partner turns, rises or changes the captured limb.

plausible: Just clasp, elbow still behind knee
Just hip frame under the opponent
trap: Just arm space, head still caught

flashcards.question: Hook Leg and Take Back (Buggy holder): What does the initial same-side arm-leg connection surround?
flashcards.answer: The original Buggy loop encloses head and arm from underneath, before any separate back-taking setup.
flashcards.answer_line: The opponent's head and one arm

plausible: Only head, both opposing arms out
One upper arm, their head outside
trap: Own thigh, their upper body outside

flashcards.question: Hook Leg and Take Back (Buggy holder): Why does hooking a leg alone not establish back control?
flashcards.answer: A lower-body hook does not itself put your chest behind the opponent or control their torso.
flashcards.answer_line: Rear torso contact is still missing

plausible: Outside leg hook acts as a seatbelt
Old loop puts sternum behind spine
trap: Ankle grip prevents turning to face

flashcards.question: Hook Leg and Take Back (Buggy holder): You pull the foot against a fixed knee. What should change?
flashcards.answer: Do not wrench the foot against the knee to preserve Buggy or manufacture a back-taking angle.
flashcards.answer_line: Release pull and unload the leg

plausible: Loosen hand, keep foot levered in
Move torso while keeping knee fixed
trap: Grip nearer toes, maintain the pull

flashcards.question: Hook Leg and Take Back (Buggy holder): What makes the first choke connection more reachable?
flashcards.answer: Turning partly onto the ribs shortens the reach between the same-side elbow and knee.
flashcards.answer_line: Frames and a partial turn onto ribs

plausible: Stay flat, extend elbow away
Extend ribs as hand reaches knee
trap: Keep shoulders flat, reach with arm

flashcards.answer: Keep the shoulders facing the opponent before a seatbelt closes.

Reach back for leg, torso unchanged

flashcards.question: Hook Leg and Take Back (defender): An arm approaches your neck after release. What do you control?
flashcards.answer: Hand fight any arm approaching the neck while maintaining a stable base.
flashcards.answer_line: The approaching arm with your hands

plausible: Low wrist as upper arm advances
Both hip hooks before the neck arm
trap: Your chin alone, allowing their grip

flashcards.question: Hook Leg and Take Back (defender): What arm position avoids easy isolation during the turn?
flashcards.answer: Keep the arm compact as you face the opponent; do not leave it separated while the new rear attack develops.
flashcards.answer_line: Elbow close to the ribs and knee

plausible: Elbow behind hip, wrist reaches back
Both arms flared beyond shoulders
trap: Elbow past knee toward their hip

flashcards.question: Hook Leg and Take Back (defender): What can occupy the space they need beside your torso?

plausible: Both knees turned away from hips
Straight arm past their far shoulder
trap: Knee outside hip, elbow held high

flashcards.question: Hook Leg and Take Back (defender): Why delay a turn while the Buggy loop still holds your head?
flashcards.answer: Clear the head-and-arm enclosure before changing direction; do not rotate through the old choke.
flashcards.answer_line: Torso can turn against trapped neck

plausible: Leg hook shifts neck load into hips
Head follows torso inside the loop
trap: Hip turn pulls the head free first
